name: ACOS
description: ACOS returns the arccosine, or inverse cosine, of a number. The result is the angle in radians whose cosine is the given number, ranging from 0 to π.
tldr: Returns the angle (in radians) whose cosine is the supplied number.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The cosine of the angle you want, which must be a real number between -1 and 1 inclusive.

basicExample.description: Find the angle whose cosine is -1
basicExample.explanation: The arccosine of -1 is π radians (180°), the angle whose cosine equals -1.

advancedExamples.title: Convert the result to degrees
advancedExamples.scenario: An engineering problem needs the angle in degrees.
advancedExamples.description: Wrap ACOS in DEGREES to read the angle in degrees.
advancedExamples.explanation: ACOS(0.5) returns π/3 radians (about 1.047), and DEGREES converts that to 60°.

advancedExamples.title: Angle of a right triangle
advancedExamples.description: Use the ratio directly as the argument.
advancedExamples.explanation: ACOS(0.6) is the angle whose cosine is 0.6, about 53.13°.

howItWorks: ACOS is the inverse of COS. For an input x in [-1, 1] it returns the unique angle θ in [0, π] (radians) such that cos(θ) = x. It uses the principal value only.

howToSteps.name: Pick the cell
howToSteps.text: Select the cell where you want the angle.

howToSteps.name: Enter the formula
howToSteps.text: Type =ACOS(number) where number is between -1 and 1.

howToSteps.name: Press Enter
howToSteps.text: The angle in radians appears; use DEGREES for degrees.

limitations: The argument must be between -1 and 1; outside that range the function returns #NUM!.
The result is always in radians, never degrees, so apply DEGREES for degree output.
ACOS returns only the principal value, so it cannot produce angles outside the [0, π] range.

commonErrors.cause: The argument is less than -1 or greater than 1.
commonErrors.fix: Ensure the value is a valid cosine between -1 and 1.
Supply a numeric value or a cell that contains a number.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ACOS works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax and behavior.

faq.question: Does ACOS return degrees?
faq.answer: No. ACOS returns radians. Multiply by 180/PI() or wrap with DEGREES to get degrees.

faq.question: What range of values does ACOS return?
faq.answer: It returns angles from 0 to π radians, i.e. 0° to 180°.

faq.question: What if I need a full-circle angle for a point?
faq.answer: Use ATAN2(x, y) instead, which returns angles across the full -π to π range using both coordinates.
